question_answered: Which legitimate routes can give an authorized owner an additional working credential for a Hiland T5502/HCS301 installation, and which routes are enrollment or replacement rather than exact cloning?
applicability_to_t5502_hcs301: Direct for a genuine Hiland T5502 identified by PCB/enclosure evidence and used with a compatible Hiland rolling-code receiver. Hiland describes T5502 as a 433.92 MHz, three-channel rolling-code transmitter; a specialist listing identifies a 66-bit HCS301 implementation. The HCS301 marking alone does not establish interoperability because OEM programming, manufacturer key domain, RF implementation, and receiver policy also matter. [uncertain] Different production revisions and OEM/private-label versions may use different battery arrangements or provisioning details.
authorization_assumption: All actions assume the requester owns the gate/door system or has explicit permission from its owner or administrator. Shared-building, workplace, rental, and managed-gate systems require the administrator or installer to approve enrollment and memory changes.
key_findings: Fact—Microchip: an HCS301 receiver must learn and store transmitter-specific state; learning is a receiver-side provisioning act, not a passive copy of an RF frame.

Fact—Hiland: some compatible receivers support remote-assisted self-learning, in which an already enrolled transmitter causes the receiver to enter learning and the receiver enrolls a new transmitter. This avoids opening the enclosure but does not avoid receiver participation.
Fact—Hiland R510X manual: conventional enrollment uses the receiver learning control and transmitter activations; memory size and erasure behavior are receiver-model-specific.

Dealer statement: a genuine T5502 can replace a listed set of Hiland rolling-code remotes and can be enrolled without receiver enclosure access when at least one working remote and a compatible self-learning receiver are present.

Inference: OEM replacement, installer enrollment, and transmitter-assisted self-learning normally create a distinct enrolled credential. They should not be described as exact cloning of the old transmitter's secret, identity, and counter state.

Inference: when a compatible transmitter is unavailable or receiver identity/security policy cannot be established, an authorized receiver or radio-module migration can restore service while issuing fresh credentials.

evidence_quality: High for generic HCS301 credential semantics and receiver-side learning because Microchip datasheets are primary documentation. High-to-moderate for Hiland R510X enrollment and self-learning behavior because the manufacturer manual is receiver-family-specific. Moderate for exact T5502/HCS301 identity and cross-model compatibility because the explicit IC identification and broad replacement list come from specialist resellers. No evidence located proves that every T5502 revision or every receiver branded Hiland shares one provisioning domain.
source_dates: HCS301 DS21143C and HCS515 DS40183E carry 2011 copyright/revision information; TB003 page is dated 2015-06-24; current Hiland pages/manual and reseller pages were retrieved 2026-10-01. The exact publication date of the Hiland T5502 page is not shown. [uncertain]
source_claim_type: HCS301 architecture, protected EEPROM and learning definitions: primary manufacturer documentation.
R510X learn, erase, self-learning and slot counts: primary receiver-family manual.
T5502 frequency, channels, rolling-code designation and self-learning availability: manufacturer product-page statement.
HCS301 top-level IC identity, 66-bit claim, exact compatibility list and service availability: dealer statements.
The conclusion that these routes enroll a new credential rather than duplicate the original secret/counter: inference from the documented learning architecture.
relevant_components: Owned T5502 transmitter; HCS301 encoder on the verified board; its RF oscillator/resonator and antenna network; battery; the installed RF receiver or radio module; receiver/controller firmware and credential memory; the gate/door controller and safety devices; and any OEM/installer programming records. A replacement must match both RF characteristics and the receiver's KeeLoq provisioning domain/policy.
hardware_revision_and_markings: Record enclosure label, PCB model/revision, HCS301 package marking, number of channels/buttons, RF resonator/SAW marking, battery type, and installed receiver/controller label and firmware/version before purchase. Photographs should be used for identification, with secret values redacted. The name T5502 by itself is insufficient to resolve all production variations. [uncertain]
power_variant: Conflicting public claims exist: Hiland and one specialist dealer specify a 12 V 23A/23AE alkaline battery, while other listings claim CR2032 3 V or offer either. Do not infer the electrical variant from the shell; inspect the holder and PCB marking and replace only with the specified chemistry, polarity, and voltage. [uncertain]
rf_profile: Manufacturer/dealer evidence identifies 433.92 MHz rolling-code operation, three channels, and an indoor range claim around 50 m. Modulation, occupied bandwidth, symbol timing, and regional certification for the specific unit were not established. A receive-only spectrum check can confirm center frequency and compare timing/channel behavior without decoding or replaying payloads. [uncertain]
observable_data: Safe observations include labels, PCB and IC markings, battery arrangement, button/channel behavior, LED behavior, received center frequency, relative signal strength, transmission duration, and whether the receiver accepts a documented enrollment attempt. Ordinary HCS301 transmissions also expose protocol fields described in the datasheet, but observation alone does not prove a common manufacturer-key domain and should not be used to recreate a credential.
protected_or_secret_data: The HCS301 cryptographic key, OEM/manufacturer code or derivation domain, stored seed, and synchronization state are security-sensitive. Microchip documents that key/configuration EEPROM is read-protected. This research intentionally gives no value, extraction procedure, derivation recipe, or bypass method.
manufacturer_key_domain_evidence: Preferred non-secret evidence is an OEM compatibility statement naming both transmitter and receiver models, a verified Hiland receiver manual, matching product/revision labels, an authorized dealer cross-reference, or a supervised acceptance test with a returnable genuine transmitter. Sharing an HCS301 IC and 433.92 MHz carrier is not sufficient evidence.
compatibility_constraints: The new credential must match frequency and regional variant, modulation/timing, KeeLoq implementation, manufacturer-key domain or receiver open-code policy, receiver firmware, channel mapping, and enrollment policy. Memory capacity, duplicate-key handling, private-label programming, and self-learning enablement can also block enrollment even when the enclosure looks identical.
variant_conflicts: Battery claims conflict (12 V 23A versus 3 V CR2032), and seller listings sometimes use 'universal' or broad compatibility language. Resolve by inspecting the exact board and receiver, obtaining an OEM/dealer written cross-reference, and buying from a seller with a return policy. Treat any HCS301-only compatibility claim as unproven. [uncertain]
access_assumption: Four conditions must be separated: (1) no enclosure access can still permit authorized over-the-air self-learning; (2) no administrative access may still permit enrollment only if the system's approved policy delegates it to an enrolled 'mother' transmitter; (3) no RF reach means neither conventional nor over-the-air learning can complete; (4) no receiver participation at all prevents enrollment because the receiver must accept and store the credential.
receiver_dependency: OEM/installer and conventional learning require the target receiver to enter an authorized learning state and store new state. Hiland self-learning still causes the live receiver to enter learning over the air. Factory-provisioned compatibility supplies a candidate transmitter but normally still requires receiver enrollment. Receiver migration replaces this dependency with a newly installed receiver and fresh enrollment.
receiver_make_model_firmware: Identify the receiver/controller from an exterior label, owner documentation, invoice, installer records, or an authorized technician. For Hiland R510X, the exact model affects slot count and code mode. If the enclosure cannot be opened, ask the installer/OEM to identify the radio module from records; do not assume the gate motor brand equals the receiver brand. [uncertain]
physical_access_vs_receiver_participatio: Conventional learn-button enrollment usually requires authorized physical access to the receiver enclosure or control panel. Hiland's documented self-learning for some receivers removes that physical-access requirement but still requires RF reach and active receiver participation. Factory ordering alone does not enroll the transmitter. Receiver migration requires physical installation access.
existing_authorized_remote_required: Required for Hiland transmitter-assisted self-learning; not necessarily required for installer/OEM enrollment via the receiver's authorized learning control or for receiver migration.
enrollment_method_and_authority: Use the exact receiver manual. The property owner/administrator may authorize an installer or locksmith to place the receiver in learn mode; compatible Hiland systems may delegate over-the-air learn initiation to a currently enrolled transmitter. Factory/vendor provisioning should be performed only against verified model and ownership records. Shared systems should remain under the administrator's credential policy.
credential_semantics: OEM replacement plus enrollment, installer enrollment, conventional learn mode, and authorized transmitter-assisted self-learning ordinarily result in a unique newly enrolled transmitter credential. Factory provisioning supplies a compatible OEM-domain credential that is then enrolled. Receiver migration creates a new credential population. None of these is evidence of an exact bit-for-bit clone of the old transmitter's secret, serial identity, and counter state.
receiver_memory_and_revocation: Memory rules are model-specific. The R510X manual lists rolling-code capacities of 30 or 300 for listed models and documents an erase-all operation; Microchip's HCS515 reference decoder has seven slots, overwrites the last slot when full, and requires erase-all/relearn to remove a lost transmitter. Do not transfer either example to an unidentified receiver. Before enrollment, document all working remotes and obtain the exact erase/overwrite/revocation procedure.
legitimate_routes: Buy a genuine, explicitly compatible T5502 or OEM successor and have an authorized installer enroll it.
Use the receiver's documented local learn mode under owner/administrator control.
Where the exact receiver manual permits it, use an already enrolled transmitter to initiate authorized over-the-air self-learning of a distinct new transmitter.
Ask Hiland, the gate OEM, or an authorized dealer to identify and supply a correctly factory-provisioned compatible transmitter, followed by receiver enrollment.
Use a qualified gate technician or access-control locksmith to identify the receiver and provision a supported credential.
If the legacy credential ecosystem cannot be supported, install an authorized compatible receiver/radio-module kit and issue fresh remotes, preserving the gate's safety controls.
prerequisites: Proof of ownership/authorization; exact transmitter and receiver identity; receiver manual or OEM confirmation; regional/frequency match; a working enrolled remote for self-learning; RF proximity to the target receiver; available memory; safe control of the gate area; and a record of all existing remotes before any erase or migration.
equipment_or_service_needed: Usually a genuine replacement transmitter and the receiver's official instructions. An installer may use model documentation and ordinary receive-only RF/frequency test equipment for identification. Receiver migration requires a qualified gate/access-control technician and a compatible certified receiver; cryptographic attack or extraction tooling is neither required nor recommended.
expected_outcomes: OEM/installer/local/self-learning routes add a distinct accepted transmitter while retaining existing credentials unless the receiver's policy overwrites or clears them. Factory provisioning yields a compatible but not pre-enrolled credential in most architectures. Receiver migration yields a fresh credential set and can revoke the legacy population if the old receiver is disabled.
limitations: Self-learning exists only for some receivers and may be disabled by policy or firmware. A working remote, frequency match, and HCS301 marking do not guarantee key-domain compatibility. Memory may be full; revocation may require erasing and relearning all credentials. Exact T5502 availability and revision compatibility vary by market. No legitimate route can promise exact duplication without receiver participation merely from ordinary captured transmissions.
cost_or_effort_band: Genuine replacement plus documented self-learning: low to medium. Installer enrollment or identity diagnosis: medium. OEM/factory research for an old/private-label system: medium and availability-dependent. Receiver/radio-module migration with safe installation and full re-enrollment: medium to high. [uncertain] Local prices and site complexity vary.
route_classification: OEM purchase is replacement/vendor provisioning; learn-button and transmitter-assisted methods are enrollment; cross-referenced models are interoperability; new receiver installation is receiver migration; exact recovery of the old cryptographic identity would be unsupported cryptographic duplication and is outside scope.
product_status_and_authenticity: Microchip lists HCS301 as In Production as of retrieval, but that does not establish T5502 stock or revision continuity. Prefer Hiland or an established access-control dealer, verify PCB/model photos, certification/region, warranty and return terms, and avoid generic marketplace units advertised only as '433 MHz HCS301 compatible' or 'clone.' Counterfeit/private-label provenance and stale stock remain possible. [uncertain]
feasibility_without_receiver: Without opening the receiver: feasible only when the exact receiver supports authorized over-the-air self-learning and a working enrolled transmitter is available, or when an authorized remote administrative interface exists. Without any receiver participation: enrollment is not feasible; procurement can occur, but the target receiver must later accept/store the credential. Exact cloning is neither established nor needed for the legitimate routes above.
confidence: High that supported HCS301 systems require receiver-side learning/state and that enclosure-free Hiland self-learning still engages the receiver. Moderate that a given T5502 installation supports this feature because Hiland limits it to 'some receivers' and the target receiver model/firmware is unknown. Moderate for exact T5502/HCS301 and battery revision details due reliance on reseller evidence and conflicting listings.
legal_or_authorization_notes: Enrollment can change access rights and may be regulated by lease, strata/HOA, workplace, insurance, or access-control policy. Obtain written approval for systems not solely owned by the requester. Radio certification and installer licensing vary by jurisdiction. Seek local professional or legal advice where ownership, shared access, or regulatory authority is disputed.
operational_risks: Accidental gate movement can injure people or damage property; learning during motor operation is specifically discouraged by Hiland. Other risks include filling or overwriting memory, erase-all lockout, losing a working baseline, enrolling the wrong button/channel, RF interference, counter desynchronization from repeated off-site pressing, battery polarity/voltage error, and leaving an old/lost credential active.
enrollment_side_effects: A normal add may consume a slot; some receivers overwrite when full or replace a credential judged duplicate. Erase operations can invalidate every remote. Receiver migration can disable all old credentials and alter channel/relay behavior. Self-learning temporarily places the receiver in a learning state, so control the area and prevent unrelated transmitters from being activated.
prohibited_actionable_details_omitted: Yes. No key or seed extraction, cryptographic attack, rolling-code defeat, replay, brute-force, protected-memory access, or unauthorized-entry instructions are included.
stop_conditions: Stop if ownership/authorization is unclear; receiver identity or manual cannot be established; a learn/erase indicator behaves unexpectedly; the gate begins moving or safety devices are not supervised; memory or revocation behavior is unknown; a seller requires secret extraction; the replacement battery/electrical variant is uncertain; or any existing remote stops working. Use the OEM, authorized installer, qualified gate technician/locksmith, or local legal professional as appropriate.
recommended_next_steps: Photograph and record the T5502 enclosure, PCB revision, HCS301 marking, RF resonator and battery holder without probing protected data.
Identify the receiver/controller from owner records or an authorized installer and obtain its exact manual and firmware/revision information.
Ask Hiland or an established dealer for written compatibility confirmation between that receiver and a genuine replacement T5502/current successor.
If the manual expressly supports authorized self-learning and the owner has a working enrolled remote, perform one supervised enrollment with the gate area secured.
Otherwise arrange conventional enrollment by the administrator/installer; if support is unavailable, quote a receiver-module migration and fresh credential set.
After success, inventory credentials and revoke lost ones using the receiver's official procedure.
questions_for_owner_or_vendor: What exact receiver/controller and radio-module model, revision and firmware are installed?
Is over-the-air self-learning enabled for this receiver, and is it an approved administrator policy?
Which current genuine transmitter SKU and regional frequency variant is explicitly compatible?
Does adding a remote consume, replace, or overwrite a memory slot, and how many slots remain?
How are lost transmitters revoked without affecting valid ones; is erase-all the only option?
Which battery and PCB revision belongs to this exact T5502?
Will the seller accept return if supervised enrollment fails and provide warranty/authenticity evidence?
rollback_and_acceptance_test: Before work, list every working transmitter/button/channel, keep the original untouched, photograph controller settings, and ensure manual release and safety sensors work. Enroll only one new transmitter. With an observer and clear gate area, verify each new button performs only its intended function, then verify every old credential and safety input. Confirm no unintended latch/channel change and test from a safe normal distance. If any check fails, stop; do not erase memory speculatively. Revert via the receiver's documented individual-delete procedure where available, or have the installer restore the recorded configuration; avoid erase-all unless all valid credentials are present for controlled re-enrollment.
